landmarks.name: Agnes Queen’s Art Gallery
facts: It is the university's public art centre, which grew out of a Kingston art and music club founded in 1926.
Its original building has been extended in 1962, 1975, 1978 and 2000.

landmarks.name: Goodes Hall
facts: It is the business school's building.
It opened in 2002, named after the family of a 1957 commerce graduate who led Warner–Lambert.

landmarks.name: The Law Building
facts: Its law school was officially established in 1957.
The university's first law faculty began in 1861 and gave an honorary degree to John A. Macdonald two years later.

landmarks.name: Louise D. Acton Building
facts: It holds a museum of health care history, in a building that celebrates nursing education in Canada.
It is a 1904 Beaux-Arts limestone building and a National Historic Site of Canada.

landmarks.name: Theological Hall
facts: People still call it the Old Arts and Science Building, and its ornate Convocation Hall hosted graduations until Grant Hall was built.
It was built in 1879, designed by Gordon & Helliwell.

landmarks.name: Grant Hall
facts: Its clock tower is the university's most famous landmark, used for convocations and exams.
It was built between 1902 and 1905.

landmarks.name: Mitchell Hall
facts: It is the newest building on campus, opened in 2018.

landmarks.name: Duncan McArthur Hall
facts: It is home to the Faculty of Education on West Campus.
The education faculty moved here by 1971.

landmarks.name: Isabel Bader Centre for Performing Arts
Victoria Hall
facts: It is the largest residence, housing nearly 900 students.
It was built in 1965.

landmarks.name: Leggett Hall
facts: It is a residence that opened in 2003; it was originally known by its address, 194 Stuart Street.

landmarks.name: Stirling Hall
facts: It is the circular physics building.
It was built in 1962 and named after a former head of the physics department.

landmarks.name: Beamish-Munro Hall
facts: It was designed as a living lab of sustainable building, with high fly-ash concrete, triple-glazed windows and solar panels.
It opened in June 2004 as the engineering faculty's newest building.

landmarks.name: Integrated Learning Centre
facts: The student-run Tea Room café opened here in the fall of 2006.

landmarks.name: Botterell Hall
facts: The health sciences library takes up two floors of it.

landmarks.name: Douglas Library
facts: It is the oldest library building on campus, with Gothic reading rooms.

landmarks.name: Mackintosh-Corry Hall
facts: It is a large social sciences complex.
It stands on the site of the original football stadium, which was torn down and moved to West Campus in 1971.

landmarks.name: Leonard Hall
facts: It is a residence named after a benefactor who donated land to the university in 1923.

landmarks.name: McLaughlin Hall
facts: It houses the mechanical engineering department.
It was a 1948 donation from the founder of General Motors of Canada.

landmarks.name: Watts Hall
facts: It is a residence that opened in 2003; it was originally known by its address, 23 Albert Street.

landmarks.name: Robert Sutherland Hall
facts: It is named after the university's first Black graduate and major benefactor.
Its dedication ceremony took place on October 3, 2009.

landmarks.name: Dunning Hall
facts: It was built during the 1950s expansion, at the same time as Richardson Hall.

landmarks.name: Richardson Hall
facts: It was built in the 1950s to house the university's administrative offices.

landmarks.name: John Deutsch University Centre
facts: Students call it the JDUC; it is the student union building, named after a former principal and economist.

landmarks.name: Fleming Hall
facts: It was the electrical engineering building, and it housed a campus radio station.
It was built in 1901 to honour the engineer who proposed standard time zones, and rebuilt after a fire in 1933.

landmarks.name: Harrison-LeCaine Hall
facts: It houses the School of Music.
It opened in 1974.

landmarks.name: Summerhill
facts: It is the oldest building on campus, opened in 1839.

landmarks.name: Clark Hall
facts: Its engineering students' pub, opened in 1971, is the oldest pub on campus.

landmarks.name: Kathleen Ryan Hall
facts: It houses both the university archives and the City of Kingston's archives.
The university archives have been here since 1981.
